hypothesis: Session load and attach-snapshot phases allocate several transient copies of the session body (whole-file String reads, parsed entry trees held alongside raw rows, deep-copied attach message trees); glibc keeps those freed pages resident per-arena for the process lifetime, so a grown session's load peak stays in RSS forever. Returning freed heap to the OS after each large transient phase + capping per-thread arenas should cut settled RSS of a loaded large session materially with no latency cost.
approach: New pa-types memory_release module: cap_thread_arenas() (mallopt M_ARENA_MAX 8) called at startup in pa-cli and pa-daemon mains; trim_freed_heap() (malloc_trim(0)) after window walk/replay in agent_engine, after worker large-frame send (trim_freed_heap_if_large >=1MiB), after create/resume and hydrated-file commands, and after the TUI attach fold; streamed line-by-line SessionFile::open (BufReader, no whole-body String); windowed store raw/metadata rows consumed in place (take_raw_entries/take_metadata_entries, retained_ids from store ids, no third parse pass); attach snapshot builds the messages tree once (moved into snapshot, non-slim top-level duplicates cloned from it); attach_data_from_response consumes the Value by move.
parity_notes: All changes are allocator plumbing and ownership moves; no data, capability, protocol, wire, prompt, or user-visible behavior changes. Non-glibc/non-Linux builds compile the helpers as no-ops (shipped platforms: Linux x86_64 glibc2.35+, Linux aarch64, macOS arm64). Attach wire bytes identical (non-slim top-level messages duplicate produced by clone of the same tree; assert tests in worker/agent_message_tests.rs + session_store_stream_tests.rs). /effort GetConnectionState wire hunk NOT present in final diff (mandatory parity restore 3c58d576b preserved through folds).
